See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Rubric percentage = Σ[(Earned ÷ Possible × 100) × Weight / 100]

A worked example

A criterion scored 8/10 at 40% weight contributes 32 percentage points. Another scored 18/20 at 60% contributes 54 points. The completed rubric grade is 86%.

Before you use the result

Include every criterion and use positive possible marks and weights. Earned marks cannot exceed possible marks. Weights must total 100%; incomplete rubrics are rejected so they are not mistaken for a final assessment result. A categorical rubric must first be converted into marks using the actual rubric rules.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Why not average earned marks directly?

Different criteria can have different maximum marks and importance. Each must first be converted to a percentage.

Can I enter an ungraded criterion as zero?

Only enter zero if it has actually been awarded. This calculator expects a completed rubric.
